title: False-negative detection → preserve state, don't reset
trigger: Detection system has false negatives (overlay covers target, nearest-match snapping) and resetting state on those false negatives causes re-trigger loops
principle: When a guard can produce false negatives (caret null due to UI overlay, geometry gate fail due to whitespace snap), don't reset state on the false negative — preserve it and only cancel pending work. State should only be cleared when there's a true positive (genuine empty space with no active target). Three guard layers must all preserve state: (1) quick check before debounce, (2) resolve failure after debounce, (3) geometry gate after resolve. Missing any one layer leaves a re-trigger path.

cases.context: Hover dictionary popup: user hovers 'machine', popup appears, user moves to whitespace gap then back to 'machine' — popup re-looks up the same word
Why pointerDelta < 6px fails: long words like 'reposition' are 60px+ wide. Moving across the word exceeds 6px but it's still the same word occurrence (same text node + same start offset).

applyFor: Any detection system with false negatives (overlay covering target, nearest-match snapping)
State machines where clearing state on ambiguous input causes re-initialization loops
